corrections.before: make_frag_sequences integer-divides total rows by fragment count, constructs exactly that many equal-sized ranges, removes floor(float rows_per_frag * ratio) alternating IDs, advances the original ID span and returns Arc sequences with fragment ordinal cast to u32. Remainder rows are dropped, num_frags=0 would divide by zero, and precision/cast behavior is inherited from f32. All later DeletionVectors are empty because removed IDs are already absent from sequences.
corrections.after: make_frag_sequences integer-divides total rows by fragment count, constructs exactly that many equal-sized ranges, requests (rows_per_frag as f32 * ratio) as usize deletions from alternating IDs, capped at the available ceil(rows_per_frag/2) candidates, advances the original ID span and returns Arc sequences with fragment ordinal cast to u32. Remainder rows are dropped, num_frags=0 would divide by zero, and precision and saturating float-to-usize cast behavior are inherited from Rust (nonnegative finite products truncate toward zero). The later constructed DeletionVector objects are empty because removed IDs are already absent from sequences. The helper cap also applies to the benchmark ratio0.8; that label is not an actual80% deletion fraction.
